newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thais seen buying 49,000 tonnes Nov-Dec soybeans.
newsitem.headline: Thais seen buying 49,000 tonnes Nov-Dec soybeans.

text.p: Thai oil crushers and feedmillers were expected to soon place orders for 49,000 tonnes of soybeans for November-December delivery, government officials and traders said on Friday.
The amount was the remainder of 426,460 tonnes of soybean import quota allowed under the government's low-tariff programme for this calendar year, according to Commerce Ministry officials.
In order to protect local soybean prices, the government allowed the beans to be imported only during January-February, June-July and November-December.
Traders and the officials said they had not heard of any order so far but anticipated some soon.
"I think they are checking prices," said one trader.
"After all, this is just September. Cargoes from Pacific Northwest will take only 25 days to arrive and it would be a bit longer from the Gulf," he said.
Soybeans imported under the government quota are levied a five-percent tariff.
